reviews.text: Austin Butler might not look much like the King, but he captures the singer's feral energy - and his singing impresses too.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: The story shows that the artist took elements from different musical styles such as gospel and blues, to fuse them with country music, rock and roll and even opera. All this through aesthetic characteristic of the director, like comics and the video clip
reviews.author: Denise Pieniazek

reviews.text: Elvis is Baz Luhrmann’s best film since Moulin Rouge!, a frantic, kinetic and incredibly captivating biopic about the King of Rock and Roll.
reviews.author: Daniel Allen

reviews.text: Director Baz Luhrmann’s sixth feature-length film “Elvis“ is officially the best superhero story of 2022.
reviews.author: Ankit Ojha

reviews.text: Elvis is a powerhouse of music, superb performances, and immaculate filmmaking. It’s a religious experience of a film. A spiritual exercise in movie making. One of the best films of the year – any year.
reviews.author: Joonatan Itkonen

reviews.text: The first twenty-some-odd minutes of this film is masterful at completely and utterly overloading the viewer.
reviews.author: Rosalie Kicks

reviews.text: Luhrmann overlooks a lot of the horrible things that happened during his legacy to create a version that is worthy of the big screen.
reviews.author: Nuha Hassan

reviews.text: There is no doubt in my mind that Elvis is a fine tribute that many fans won't regret watching, but it just gets in its own way and doesn't manage to stand as an exceptional one.
reviews.author: Emma-Jane Betts

reviews.text: The film gets in its way but is a good start for Butler’s growing career.
reviews.author: Jillian Chilingerian

reviews.text: The triumph of Elvis comes in the form of lead actor Austin Butler, who embodies the King from start to finish. Butler's performance brings life to an often cartoonish man, selling his soul to director Baz Luhrmann's trademark flash and flair.
reviews.author: Matthew Creith

reviews.text: Elvis is a strong effort from everyone involved, and is worth watching for Butler alone; he is a star. It's a wild ride that will undoubtedly provide fun, laughter and toe-tapping happiness.
reviews.author: Rebecca Johnson

reviews.text: Colonel Parker describes Elvis as “the greatest show on earth.” If Butler’s performance manages to capture even an ounce of Elvis’ magic, Colonel Parker might just have been right.
reviews.author: Tina Kakadelis

reviews.text: Austin Butler stars in a sensory experience so flashy and grandiose that it can only be described by the feeling it evokes: nausea.
reviews.author: Ryan Oquiza

reviews.text: It also shows Luhrmann continuing to swing for the fences. His "Elvis" captures the enormity of this pop culture phenomenon, with enough chutzpah to overcome the bumps in the road.
reviews.author: Rubén Rosario

reviews.text: Here’s the key problem: there are effectively two films playing out at the same time.
reviews.author: Grant Watson

reviews.text: There’s just no reason for its nearly 160-minute runtime; but the music is fantastic.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: Butler here is a co-auteur in a way usually closed to biopics in which the lead actors are more famous than Butler is, and so we never lose them in their roles as other famous people.
reviews.author: A.S. Hamrah

reviews.text: Another flat one sided look at a rock idol that’s never bold enough to challenge our perceptions of them.
reviews.author: Felix Vasquez Jr.

reviews.text: Rarely do we see a performance that is so electric that as soon as the film gets over, one rushes to search about the actor instead.
reviews.author: Santanu Das

reviews.text: A dazzling opulence of color, set design, and musical presentations.
reviews.author: Steve Crum

reviews.text: Butler’s explosive interpretation of Elvis – from the physical gesticulations to the big, burly voice – humanized The King, pulling down the bright lights to show us the distressed man behind the immortal God of Rock.
reviews.author: Mark Johnson

reviews.text: ...a disappointing misfire that squanders its host of appealing attributes.
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: The story of the King has been told many times, but nothing like Baz Luhrmann's sensational, impressionistic take on Elvis Presley (played with pitch-perfect resonance by an explosively charismatic Austin Butler).
reviews.author: Dann Gire

reviews.text: Austin Butler blew us all away as Elvis and still is.
reviews.author: Fletcher Peters

reviews.text: Elvis has one of the best lead performances this year from Austin Butler. The singing, the set design, the recreation of iconic moments, and the engaging performances are insane! Hanks plays one of the most despising characters he's ever attempted also!
reviews.author: Samuel Leggett Jr.

reviews.text: Let’s just give Austin Butler his Best Actor Oscar now. This young man has range to spare. Wow!
reviews.author: Cole Smithey

reviews.text: "Elvis may be the most Baz Lurhmann, Baz Lurhmann has ever been. And it’s hard to imagine there’s any way for him to top himself from here."
reviews.author: Cate Young

reviews.text: A bravura return to form from the country’s most extra filmmaker, Baz Luhrmann’s full-throttle biopic of the King is almost entirely devoid of silence, mainlining the greatest hits fused surprisingly delicately with contemporary tracks
reviews.author: Stephen A. Russell

reviews.text: In typical Luhrmann fashion, he grossly overcompensates with his self-indulgent trademarks like cheap visual tactics used ad nauseam. It’s maximalist entertainment at its worst.
reviews.author: Eric Marchen

reviews.text: “This is Butler’s interpretation of Elvis. This isn’t an actor impersonating Elvis, which I think is really key.”
reviews.author: Raquel Stecher

reviews.text: There are certainly no half measures here. Not one single thing is subdued or understated here. One’s tolerance for the in-your-face, OTT theatrics will greatly depend on your enjoyment of Luhrmann’s previous efforts.
reviews.author: Dallas King

reviews.text: Thrillingly, director Baz Luhrmann makes the remarkable response to the singer feel like the only possible option to being offered this much pleasure, this much freedom.
reviews.author: Charles Taylor

reviews.text: Elvis is an operatic creation, one that is over-the-top and messy in places, yet in a way that suits its larger-than-life subject. It's all anchored by a stunning lead performance from Austin Butler, who breathes new life into Elvis.
reviews.author: Audrey Fox

reviews.text: Elvis Presley has a song in which he requests, “A little less conversation, a little more action, please,” but this film needed just the opposite.
reviews.author: Asia Frey

reviews.text: It is at its best when Luhrmann's cinematic eccentricities are let loose and he leans into the raucous performances. Regrettably, the experience overall becomes far less than the sum of its parts.
reviews.author: Chase Hutchinson

reviews.text: Baz Luhrmann and Elvis Presley should be a match made in showmanship heaven. But, "Elvis" is too incongruous. Luhrmann injects his flair, but less cogent and thoughtful. It is awash in its own ambivalence about what it wants to say, or why.
reviews.author: Andrew Kendall

reviews.text: There’s no shortage of entertaining scenes, but it’s a sure sign of creative failure when the character Tom Hanks most resembles isn’t Colonel Tom Parker but rather the gluttonous Mr. Creosote from Monty Python’s The Meaning of Life.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: On the whole, the film is a fine spectacle. ... But once the spell is broken, we can see the strings and puppet shows lose their luster when they run two hours+.
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: Butler nails Presley’s husky voice and physical mannerisms like his wiggle with great control always humanizing Presley every step of the way.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: Pretty visuals and an outstanding performance from Butler do not save the film. Struggles with the screenplay, the bad performance from Hanks, and ignorance about Presley's relationship with black music undermine the more substantial discourse of Elvis.
reviews.author: Alan French

reviews.text: Hitting deep notes and shaking right, Butler gives us a film delight.
reviews.author: Betty Jo Tucker

reviews.text: Far from the visual notes that are already a stylistic hallmark of the director, I find the way in which he reduces Elvis's iconography to moments of fireworks dull and too frivolous. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: Luhrmann’s biofilm is more like an Elvis impersonator -- bloated and bejeweled, barely skimming the surface of one of the most original entertainers who ever lived.
reviews.author: Eleanor Ringel Cater

reviews.text: Luhrmann appropriates the idea of Elvis to manifest himself... and connects us with the best version of Elvis. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: It's all very stylized and flashy and modern, self-consciously hip in a way that's clearly been designed to speak to generations for whom Elvis Presley may not be the King of Rock 'n' Roll so much as the guy on the soundtrack to "Lilo & Stitch."
reviews.author: Ed Masley

reviews.text: Elvis is not bad, pretty good even, but not very good, and never great.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: A dazzling portrait of Elvis’s life and career that reveals the roots of his appeal.
reviews.author: Frederic and Mary Ann Brussat

reviews.text: For both the uninitiated and the hardcore Elvis fans this is a solid biopic that evolves into an analysis about what it actually meant to be a super star in the 20th century, a culture icon. Before Internet, Social Media and influencers.
reviews.author: Alejandro Turdó

reviews.text: This biopic is all show and very little tell--a lifeless story that cannot be rescued by the impressive visuals and the strong performances
reviews.author: J. Don Birnam

reviews.text: Those of you wanting more about Elvis' process or, frankly, the art itself will therefore be disappointed. This tragedy is about control. The music's secondary.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: Austin Butler is entrancing as Elvis. His performance alone is why anyone should watch this movie.
reviews.author: Susan Kamyab

reviews.text: A blitzkrieg of pop art
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: Luhrmann has managed to capture the essence of the legendary Elvis Presley, in the form of what can only be called a tragic success story.
reviews.author: Monica Reid

reviews.text: ...it’s grabby and it prowls; and it does have something to say, even if by the end it’s saying it a little too carefully...
reviews.author: Eve Tushnet

reviews.text: A flashy, stylized biopic fitting of the King.
reviews.author: Sean Chandler

reviews.text: The pure entertainment of the musical numbers make the film an eye-opening and fascinating watch.
reviews.author: Nick Boyd

reviews.text: “Wise men say only fools rush in,” Elvis Presley sang. Director Baz Luhrmann should have taken those words to heart, as almost all he does in Elvis, his new whirlwind of a musical bio-pic, is rush.
reviews.author: Cameron Meier

reviews.text: I am sure when Oscar nomination time comes, there will be nominations here for Austin Butler and Tom Hanks and the soundtrack.
reviews.author: Marie Asner

reviews.text: Elvis manifests all its action as inevitable, a remembered history that seems to have never breathed as living present: a most unquestioning sort of remembrance.
reviews.author: George Elkind

reviews.text: n spite of the narrative flaws the film may have, the musical numbers are captivating, and no one could have better captured the essence of the character than Luhrman. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Gisela Savdie

reviews.text: A standardized musical biopic with a few authorial strokes, though with an identifying feature that makes this film a must-see and that is its protagonist [Austin Butler]. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rafael Santisteban

reviews.text: Presley was larger than life — he is still larger than life — but Butler takes the myth and makes him a man once again.
reviews.author: Ashley Marie

reviews.text: Luhrmann's tendency to hyperbolize has previously caused fatigue, but in this instance it's an adequate vehicle to tell the rise and fall story of an extravagant idol. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Leonardo Garcia Tsao

reviews.text: Austin Butler, almost feral with his presence, is a perfect fit for this bombastic odyssey. He kills it.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Zhang

reviews.text: This movie is going to make people who have a certain picture of Elvis in their mind happy. Luhrmann was very careful to make a movie in service to the legacy of Elvis but this felt less like a biopic and more like a story about his manager.
reviews.author: Ro Moore

reviews.text: In addition to the flamboyance that glazes at the surface, the film suffers from a certain artificiality that removes emotional heft. We sense that something is not right.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: Even though Luhrmann seems really interested in all the existencial details, they end up sacrificed on the altar of pretension. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Marcelo Stiletano

reviews.text: Elvis doesn't start with Elvis, but with Colonel Parker. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: What Baz Luhrmann has done is to transfer that exciting emotion of the past to a present where, with the help of other elements and codes of this time, it is very clear to us why Elvis Presley is a legend.  [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Angel H. Mora

reviews.text: Crazy in the best sense of the word: it's a roller coaster of music, colors and hyperbolic performances.  [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Arturo Mora

reviews.text: Austin Butler is a star.
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: An extremely energetic film, which needed to be extremely fast-paced and stylised in order to tell a long story in just over two and a half hours. Full review in Spanish.
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: Less of a biopic than glittery Gatsby style party, the new movie Elvis explodes with energy and excitement.
reviews.author: Robin Holabird

reviews.text: "Colorful, flashy, loud, full of music, and giant bursts of energy, which describes the singer's life pretty well. Of course it wouldn't work without the right person playing The King himself and they found him in Austin Butler."
reviews.author: Paul Salfen

reviews.text: A film that’s more gimmick than effective, remaining superficial… without a soul.  [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Hugo Hernández Valdivia

reviews.text: This film is exhausting, but Austin Butler is the saving grace of it all.
reviews.author: Josie Meléndez

reviews.text: Though largely chronological, Luhrmann’s film is less about “this leads to that” storytelling as it is about iconic moments—defining phases and turning points in the artist’s life and career.
reviews.author: Brett McCracken

reviews.text: Gaudy, glitzy, histrionic, relentlessly ADHD and dumb as dirt, but as a musical biopic thrill-ride it's kind of okay.  (It almost feels like it was directed by an alternate-universe Michael Bay who's queer).
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: Austin Butler seems possessed by the king's spirit, flooding the screen with irresistible charm and primal physicality.
reviews.author: Nestor Bentancor

reviews.text: Elvis is hyperbolic, one-dimensional and ludicrous – but as high-excess cinematic myth-making, it’s a blast.
reviews.author: Jonathan Romney

reviews.text: Austin Butler is so effective in his musical performances it was just like watching Elvis himself. This movie is a fitting tribute to Elvis the entertainer, as well as a damning indictment of racism and corruption in America.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: One of the more impressive, energetic and fantastical films of the crowded and clichéd genre.
reviews.author: Nicolás Delgadillo

reviews.text: It's only in the second half, when Luhrmann calms down, that the film truly engages, and Butler's stunning performance is able to shine through and become more than just a caricature.
reviews.author: Matt Neal

reviews.text: Luhrmann's fast-cutting super-montage style overpowers the subject matter, and the result is an impressionistic, jumbled highlight reel of Presley’s many accomplishments, despite vivid recreations by actor Austin Butler as The King.
reviews.author: Todd Gilchrist

reviews.text: Luhrmann's great comeback, gorges without causing indigestion, derails without losing the storyline, and entertains with a story that even though it's deciphered from the beginning, never offers a dull moment. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Emiliano Basile

reviews.text: Elvis is fantastic. Austin Butler melted into the Elvis role and by the end, the line between film and reality blurred. Expect Butler to be the frontrunner this upcoming awards season for Best Actor. Brilliantly directed by Baz Luhrmann.
reviews.author: Sheraz Farooqi

reviews.text: It’s big and bold and brassy. It’s not perfect, and at 2 hours and 39 minutes still doesn’t deliver everything you’d expect in a telling of Elvis’s life story. But it’s always holding your attention.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: While I like the movie, and Butler is excellent, Hanks is miscast and flailing a bit in this one.
reviews.author: Bob Grimm

reviews.text: Butler is spot-on as the King, and Luhrman not only brings the music to life, he adds a contemporary flair to some songs by blending in hip-hop. Most importantly, the filmmaker contextualizes each song with Elvis’ life.
reviews.author: Alan Ng

reviews.text: If you have come to this film expecting new insights or revelations, then you will find there is nothing to see here. Actually, there is something to see, but it is of course all the fireworks and glitter of a Baz Luhrmann film dealing with Elvis.
reviews.author: Louie Fecou

reviews.text: Baz Luhrmann IS Col. Tom Parker. An exploitive carnival barker endlessly shouting at you but saying nothing. Completely wrapped up in his own voice that none other can get through, snatching your money and giving you nothing to take with you in return.
reviews.author: Erik Childress

reviews.text: "Elvis" rocks.
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: The performance by Butler is near perfect; the performance by Tom Hanks grows on you; the directing style of Luhrman is significant and easily distinguishable.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: The new biopic of the King does what’s totally unnecessary: clumsily bury the legend of Elvis under devices and metaphors.
reviews.author: Paul Thompson

reviews.text: At 159 minutes, it would be almost redundant to point out that Elvis is an indulgent piece of work...
reviews.author: Jon Negroni

reviews.text: Opulent and over-the-top, dazzling and dizzy, this new Baz Luhrmann biopic-fantasia never takes us closer to Elvis the man, but, wow, it sure understands Elvis the spectacle.
reviews.author: Alison Gillmor

reviews.text: Austin Butler has more in common with Elvis besides his gorgeous looks; both were the same tender age (23) when their mothers' died; thus giving Butler a deeper connection due to their shared profound loss, which, in turn garnered a heartfelt performance.
reviews.author: Sarah Knight Adamson

reviews.text: Baz Luhrmann turns the life of Elvis Aaron Presley into a three-ring circus with more sensation than sense in Elvis. But it’s got a good beat and you can dance to it.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: Baz Luhrmann’s Elvis tries to sell audiences on a sanitized version of the King, missing the much weirder, wilder, and messier truth of his life and career.
reviews.author: Eileen Jones

reviews.text: Flashes of color, lightning cuts, and the camera spins and needle drops are at times overwhelming, but it’s an overall enjoyable experience that washes over you in waves of excitement.
reviews.author: Adam Mullins-Khatib

reviews.text: The film is flawed, makes some baffling choices, and takes every one of Luhrmann’s directorial tics and turns them up to full volume, but as long as Elvis is on stage, the movie is massively entertaining.
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: Elvis is a dazzling journey into Elvis the man and Elvis the phenomenon, dusting off his  now dated brand of Rock and Roll and making it feel fresh and vital.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: This Elvis, despite some attempts to get the formula all shook up, provides as much commentary on its subject as most biopics do for theirs; that is to say, not much at all.
reviews.author: Abby Olcese

reviews.text: Luhrmann shows just enough restraint and as a result, we get a film that brilliantly captures Elvis' outer grandeur but also his inner demons. Call it an exhilarating cinematic portrait of triumph and tragedy.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: It’s the “wiggle” that gets your attention in “Elvis.” But it’s the swagger and strut of Austin Butler, bumping and grinding his way through a star-making turn as Elvis “the Pelvis” Presley, that gets you all shook up...
reviews.author: Dana Barbuto

reviews.text: A musical biopic as filtered through the lens of a superhero epic.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: With [Austin] Butler on-screen and [director Baz] Luhrmann behind the camera, the King lives on.
reviews.author: Candice McMillan

reviews.text: Only the sixth feature from Baz Luhrmann whose work has been uniquely spectacular though without that much to chew on, but Elvis delivers in so many ways with terrific lead performances, stunning art production and cinematography, and is his tour de force
reviews.author: Jane Freebury

reviews.text: By the end you genuinely feel the artist never really got to achieve his vision of connecting with gospel and soul more deeply, and touring the world, because of Parker’s gaslighting and control.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: The first half of the film burns with a visual intensity that’s as irresistible as Elvis was. But then we have to suffer through the second half.
reviews.author: Beth Accomando

reviews.text: Baz Luhrmann photobombs this Elvis portrait with over-extravagant filmmaking that dwarfs the iconic rock and roller. And that ain’t easy.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: 'Elvis' promises something it's unable to deliver, choosing to be a spectacle and caricaturing its protagonists to delirium... Luhrmann refuses to throw shade and paint the gray areas. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Randy Meeks

reviews.text: An all-out assault on the senses that can shatter the will of even pro athletes, director Baz Luhrmann’s Elvis biopic is so unbearable that it makes a strong case for why studios should always retain some oversight over auteurs.
reviews.author: Rohan Naahar

reviews.text: Maybe a Baz / Elvis mini-series would have been more my speed.
reviews.author: Kent Garrison

reviews.text: A good Baz Luhrmann film. It's also a pretty good Elvis Presley film, for that matter, and it's a little bit surprising that those  two things aren't more directly in conflict with each other.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: While the film is sensorily splendiferous, it is also narratively unambitious, from its linear approach to its framing device.
reviews.author: Neil Morris

reviews.text: It’s both fun and yet more of an introduction, bold yet overlong. What can’t be called is boring, which is fitting because that could rarely be said about Elvis Presley.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: This is a spectacle, a colourful mural clad in fairy lights for a generation who missed the real thing.
reviews.author: Hilary A White

reviews.text: The film’s attitude to Presley’s music is perplexing — hardly a single song is played in full and those we do hear are thrown away in gimmicky overlays.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: Colourfully assembled with whizzy camerawork, effects and editing, the film is strikingly well-performed and features fantastic musical sequences.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: With Baz Luhrmann pairing his unique talents as a director with a fantastic crew and a stunning lead performance by Austin Butler, Elvis is a captivating and haunting feature that does the legendary figure right.
reviews.author: Carson Timar

reviews.text: As an Elvis biopic, Elvis lacks. But as an exciting way for teens to get a taste of how "the good ol' days" weren't as "good" as some want to remember, it's ideal.
reviews.author: Tara McNamara

reviews.text: Austin Butler gives the performance of the year in Elvis. The film is a maximalist masterpiece from director Baz Luhrmann, a sheer exhibition of the man’s penchant for exuberant style.
reviews.author: Maxance Vincent

reviews.text: Elvis may well be Luhrmann’s best and most commercial film to date.
reviews.author: Wade Major

reviews.text: A handsomely-mounted production that's entertaining, if not exactly revelatory.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: Its framing device strangles the life from the film and restricts it to being what it’s trying to shirk: the traditional tragic story of a man consumed by fame and fortune.
reviews.author: Christopher Cross

reviews.text: Even with its flaws, Elvis is a compelling and distinctive portrait of fame and its deadly trappings. It’s also Luhrmann’s vision of America, which encapsulates a melting pot-like beauty under a dark capitalist shadow.
reviews.author: Chad Byrnes

reviews.text: Austin Butler is Baz Luhrmann’s Tulpa. Luhrmann conceived him and drapes him in a halo of devastating beauty. Butler can sing, dance and appears possessed in ecstasy by the soul of Elvis.
reviews.author: Victoria Alexander

reviews.text: Elvis won’t really tell you anything more than you already know about Presley either. It’s not an in-depth look at his psyche or his ground-breaking career. It is, however, an ode to African American culture and its impact on current pop culture.
reviews.author: Amelia Harvey

reviews.text: There’s undoubtedly a story to be told about the life of Elvis, but this version will leave you wishing for a softer touch, in a movie that is all shook up.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: Baz Luhrmannn’s “Elvis” is a bloated, glitzy, behind-the-music biopic that makes no pretense about pandering.
reviews.author: Noah Berlatsky

reviews.text: An enthralling, albeit wildly inconsistent, odyssey through Elvis’ trailblazing journey.
reviews.author: Matt Conway

reviews.text: “Elvis” is a sumptuous visual experience, packed with great music and an excellent titular performance...a compelling and captivating musical biopic, albeit one that perhaps could have used a little less conversation and a little more action.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: The most anachronistic element of Elvis is its cloying need to assure us that its hero was a good person, as if trying to preemptively counter some imagined onslaught of TikToks about why Elvis Presley is problematic.
reviews.author: Jack Hamilton

reviews.text: Of the actors who have previously tried to bottle Elvis’s lightning-like magic, none has come close to the physical, emotional, electrical energy that throbs through Austin Butler’s titular performance here.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: It’s an epic collage of images and sensations, but it is not a movie. Yet despite a surfeit of annoying flaws, I must add that it is also an occasional whale of an extravaganza.
reviews.author: Rex Reed

reviews.text: I'm far from a Presley fan, but Luhrmann's film left me all shook up, and in love, uh-huh.
reviews.author: Toby Woollaston

reviews.text: Luhrmann's movie achieves its goals of highlighting Elvis' music while providing a capable, if imperfect, abstract of his life. For fans of the icon and his music, it hits enough sweet spots to be worthy of a theatrical viewing.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: Luhrmann throws decades of music history into a blender, emphasizing what it must have felt like to see Elvis in the early '50s, rather than what it actually sounded like.
reviews.author: Alex Hudson

reviews.text: I can’t deny that I had a fun time watching it, but I also spent a lot of the too-long running time rolling my eyes. It’s a Baz Luhrmann film. What else were we to expect?
reviews.author: Kayleigh Donaldson

reviews.text: I joked with my friend that this is going to be white folks’ Belly—you could watch Elvis without sound and still be captivated.
reviews.author: Julian Lytle

reviews.text: Submerges us in a spiraling, compulsive and frenetic epic that envelops us in an embrace, and shakes and pulses to the beat of the making and the deconstruction of one of the biggest icons in popular culture... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Beatriz Martínez

reviews.text: In the end, though, the sheer force of personality at work in this film is enough to make it live up to the hype. “Elvis” is, like the man himself, an experience of sensory overload that you won’t soon forget.
reviews.author: Matthew Jackson

reviews.text: Elvis is propelled forward — almost maniacally so — by Presley’s music... The relentless music makes the whole thing feel like a montage...  But it’s infectious.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: It can feel like an example of style over substance. However, the film finds its storytelling legs as it proceeds and presents a relatively interesting portrayal of a man who changed music.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: Baz Luhrmann's gaudy extravaganza is spectacular yet strangely sad. Austin Butler delivers an amazing Elvis impersonation, while Tom Hanks - camouflaged under mounts of latex - epitomizes creepy con-man Col. Tom Parker.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: Any tension from Presley’s real-life struggles is forsaken for flashes of pizzazz but the career-defining turn of its young lead actor is a highlight–it will be hard for anybody this year to top Austin Butler.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: Elvis is pure fairy floss – sickly sweet, colourful, and quick to melt into nothingness.
reviews.author: John McDonald

reviews.text: Thanks to ELVIS, the King will NEVER leave the building!
reviews.author: Michael A. Smith

reviews.text: Elvis is a 159-minute atomic blast of rhinestone glory.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: Anchored by a powerful performance by Austin Butler, "Elvis" casts the The King of Rock and Roll as an unwitting mark in a carnival side show act. Hank's Colonel Parker is annoying, but Butler is a brand new star.
reviews.author: Mark Jackson

reviews.text: The perfect apotheosis of the Elvis myth.
reviews.author: Andrea Chase

reviews.text: The film is a structural failure. Butler, who pours his heart and soul into every moment, deserves so much more.
reviews.author: Michael Ward

reviews.text: Austin Butler is phenomenal in Baz Luhrmann's rock biopic as the titular king of rock and roll in...Elvis.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: Elvis isn’t going to please those looking for a more nuanced take on the legend or something that bucks the formula of the musician biopic, but as a crowd-pleasing epic it hits every note like a pro.
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: An overlong, overproduced, headache-inducing biopic with excessive style over substance. It's a nearly 3-hour music video masquerading as a movie.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: The world is more plentiful with filmmakers like Luhrmann infusing their signature style into them, but “Elvis” stutters and starts more often then it captivates.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: Using his signature flash and high style, Luhrmann focuses on a few angles that make the King feel fresh again, so much so that even newcomers may be awakened to his music.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: Butler will leave you All Shook Up, but ’Elvis’ could have used A Little Less Conversation.  Maybe a lot less.
reviews.author: Jeff Mitchell

reviews.text: Austin Butler delivers a marvelous performance in this sparkling and extravagant spectacle about the life and career of the beloved King of Rock and Roll. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: "This big screen take on the King is both too much and not enough."
reviews.author: Kip Mooney

reviews.text: I enjoyed the performance of Austin Butler as Presley but could not fully wrap my head around Hanks’ portrayal of Parker. ...  Hanks .. cannot go as dark as he should in his presentation. He still exudes hints of the Hanks likability and charm ...
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: Focus in this film was wrong … does anybody care that Hanks-as-Col-Parker stole his money … E still had his own plane. Hanks interpretation of Parker was unimpressive, I don’t he understood the character. BUT Austin Butler was sensational as E! Yeah Baby!
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: Butler understands his character’s struggle and the demons that would later consume Presley. His public persona is that of a charming fellow. Butler nails it. He also walks like Elvis in a way that is eerie. The movie never feels unrealistic.
reviews.author: Michael Calleri

reviews.text: Through almost every minute of this lengthy, ever-rocking epic, you'll rarely pull your eyes away from Austin Butler, the 30-year-old actor who seriously becomes a star by embodying one of the brightest of all time.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: At nearly two hours, forty minutes, many will be compelled to compare the film’s bloated runtime to the singer’s late-career physique. But what is too long when you’re having a blast?
reviews.author: Frank Wilkins

reviews.text: The filmmakers get high marks for the pacing, and musical choices. More so than all previous Presley movies, “Elvis” devotes a good stretch of time to his dirt poor childhood and the effect that blues, country, and especially gospel would have on him.
reviews.author: Michael Clark

reviews.text: ELVIS is Baz Luhrmann’s love letter to the King of Rock and Roll. It’s loud, frenetic, waaaaay too long, but ultimately highly entertaining.
reviews.author: Jeanne Kaplan

reviews.text: It doesn’t matter if you were president of the Elvis Presley fan club  or just a casual music fan, ELVIS is a must-see for the indelible performances by Hanks and especially Butler.
reviews.author: David Kaplan

reviews.text: ELVIS is too dizzying even by Baz Luhrmann's standards, but thankfully Austin Butler’s star power and astounding performance still shine through. He manages to rise above all the glitz and discombobulating spectacle.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: [A] ravishing big screen experience.
reviews.author: Glenn Dunks

reviews.text: Elvis is an irresistible sensation of music and style that serves as a flashy flick fit for a king. The musical performances will obviously be a major draw but the stellar performances make it all the more intoxicating.
reviews.author: Mark McPherson

reviews.text: It is absurdly entertaining. Embodies everything I like and dislike about Baz Luhrmann.
reviews.author: Andy Klein

reviews.text: A wildly over-the-top and extremely entertaining biopic of Elvis Presley.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: Austin Butler doesn’t just portray Elvis, he frees Elvis from decades of chintz and tragedy. He gives Elvis back to us.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: Luhrmann bets on the greatest hits, the epic moments of [Elvis'] life and so we're always beholding the myth, the bronze, the legend, and not the man in the flesh. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: Austin Butler is amazing as Elvis, but the film itself feels like a somber artsy documentary with a narrator you pretty much despise.
reviews.author: Derek Sante

reviews.text: Visually stunning and flamboyant with a fantastic performance by Austin Butler, it suffers from a bloated running time and some character misdirections.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: Among the many things this film does is reinforce the true unknowability of American icons.
reviews.author: Tyler Smith

reviews.text: Misguided attempts to jam both Presley and Parker's stories into one cohesive mix was a gamble for any filmmaker, but even Baz couldn't pull it off.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: Luhrmann is preoccupied, understandably, with situating Elvis within his historical context. In doing so, however, he discards the more interesting story.
reviews.author: Hannah Engler

reviews.text: It's a biography of who we could be vs. who we are. We could be heroes if only we weren't sloppy, addicted, venal, and sedated, it says. We could be heroes.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: More somatic threat than motion picture, Baz Luhrmann’s Elvis—the rhinestoned belt buckle of musical biopics—is like a sneeze into a bullhorn: Incoherent at volcanic decibels.
reviews.author: Saffron Maeve

reviews.text: A frenetic tour of The King’s dizzying rise and steep fall.
reviews.author: Nandini Ramnath

reviews.text: Elvis, in the epic tradition of all of Luhrmann’s work, is a brash, overwhelming experience... It’s too much. Yet if it were any less excessive, it wouldn’t be as doggedly effective as it often is.
reviews.author: K. Austin Collins

reviews.text: Through Luhrmann’s lens, Elvis transforms from someone striking and fresh to a relic clinging for relevancy in a changing world. Luhrmann presents the familiar narrative with enough verve to make it feel new.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: Baz Luhrmann brilliantly floods our senses with arresting sights and sounds.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: When the velvet Elvis painting becomes fact, shoot the velvet.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: This shameless cultural jumble might make some kind of crazy sense for anyone who still thinks Presley the figurehead of pop vulgarity. That position has many successors, and Luhrmann is one of them.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: It’s a credit to Butler’s performance that this film nearly works in spite of all the fatal flaws piling up around him. But even a spectacular performance like this can’t save a film crippled by Luhrmann’s bombastic direction.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: At its best Elvis is a kinetic fever-dream fantasia on rock’s most enduring icon, with newcomer Austin Butler portraying The King in such convincing style that there are moments when I wasn’t sure if I was watching an actor or old footage of the real man.
reviews.author: Robert W. Butler

reviews.text: The electricity coursing through the best scenes is what the shared big-screen experience is all about.
reviews.author: Harry Guerin

reviews.text: The two-and-a-half hours of Elvis will fly by with incredible vigour.
reviews.author: Dhaval Roy

reviews.text: Say what you want to about him, the man who sang “Don’t Be Cruel” and “Are You Lonesome Tonight?” was a unique and magnetic phenomenon when he came on the scene. The movie that bears his name feels all too ordinary.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: Call my reaction "mixed." Elvis can't be called deep or definitive, but there's plenty to enjoy in the story of a star who couldn't stand still and a movie that follows suit.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: Baz Luhrmann’s big swing at the King’s life is a thrilling theatrical spectacle.
reviews.author: Oli Welsh

reviews.text: I don't understand how people either like it or hate it. I watch it without being provoked emotionally one way or another. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Boyero

reviews.text: Elvis is a beautiful, flawed, tragic movie about a beautiful, flawed, tragic human being.
reviews.author: Collin Garbarino

reviews.text: Butler’s entire performance is grounded with heart-wrenching emotional depth. That is, unfortunately, just about the only good thing I can say about Elvis, which is as glitzed-out and overstuffed as you’d expect from a Luhrmann film, but not in a fun way.
reviews.author: Vivian Kane

reviews.text: A loud, bombastic biopic that sidesteps most of the difficult questions surrounding Elvis' life to instead focus on the graft at the core of popular music's enduring spectacle.
reviews.author: Dominic Griffin

reviews.text: There’s still enough of a fascinating story here to paper over some of the film’s shortcomings, and it conveys something of Presley’s musical and personal magnetism, but it should have been more than this. It won’t do Austin Butler any harm, though.
reviews.author: Adam Sweeting

reviews.text: Baz Luhrmann’s best movie since his masterpiece Romeo + Juliet is brilliant but overlong, and Tom Hanks masterfully wrestles with a flubbed role as con-man manager Colonel Tom Parker. But Austin Butler is an utter wonder as Elvis.
reviews.author: Tim Appelo

reviews.text: Something of a mess, filmwise... but something of that over-the-top style actually works to help explain how such a devout, modest little kid growing up dirt-poor in the south, could become the most famous entertainer in the world.
reviews.author: Piers Marchant

reviews.text: A showbizzy Passion Play stuffed with sequins.
reviews.author: Robert Horton

reviews.text: It’s clear Luhrmann is more interested in mythmaking, era-hopping, and genre-melding than he is in trying to dig all that deeply into the complex cultural, racial, and political realities of Presley’s life.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: Memorable and exciting if not what you might call deep; it’s a bit too whiz-bang, too full of itself and its mischievous glories to be taken seriously... Lurhman obviously put his heart and hormones into making Elvis, but relax, Baz!
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: A narratively rich and propulsive story.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: For all its slick surface pleasures, this wild ride through the life and career of The King winds up providing little insight that couldn’t be found on a placard at Graceland.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: A perfect marriage of artistry and kitsch. A movie about Elvis told like it's an Elvis movie.
reviews.author: Doug Walker

reviews.text: Beyond Luhrmann’s take on cultural appropriation versus appreciation, the film also looks into how fame is a drug — like actual drugs, can stunt your mental growth to stay stuck at the age of your first hit.
reviews.author: Diandra Reviews

reviews.text: Elvis was never in the Building
reviews.author: Kathia Woods

reviews.text: It's a bit of a spectacle, not quite life-changing but larger-than-life...a whirlwind of flashing lights, gaudy costumes and shaking hips.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: I liked it, though my corneas did feel a little crunchy afterward.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: ELVIS, directed by the wonderfully flashy Baz Luhrmann, is as glitzy and dazzling as Elvis Presley himself. Austin Butler knocks it out of the park in this brilliant, star-making performance.
reviews.author: Lauren Bradshaw

reviews.text: Swept up in the glint of the leather and the bejeweled jumpsuits, Luhrmann overlooks the messy human who hid underneath. And so, he misses out on the heart that could have made his film truly spectacular.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: Every surface is cleanly wiped. Every fabric seems fresh out of the box. There is no journey to Vegas. We are essentially there from the opening scene.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: Butler captures the conflicted soul of a man who conquered the world but died alone on a bathroom floor in Memphis.
reviews.author: Kurt Loder

reviews.text: Baz Luhrmann’s bejeweled battering ram of a biopic is all over the place, which  can be distracting, but the grit and grace of Austin Butler’s performance as The King is a thing of beauty. A star is born right here.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: The film is beautiful & has an electric energy, especially during Elvis’ performances, but it can't maintain the same enthusiasm it started with.
reviews.author: Mae Abdulbaki

reviews.text: This films needs big screen, a good sound system and the mood to be engulfed in one man's journey to the top as he's helped and hindered by manipulative friend.  Austin Butler is amazing as The King and Tom Hanks is excellent as a polite villain.
reviews.author: Jana Monji

reviews.text: It is a gamble that does not exactly pay off, in no small part because Tom Hanks plays Tom Parker, and the performance is the low point of his career.
reviews.author: Alan Zilberman

reviews.text: Some might be left frustrated by the modern fairy tale’s avoidance of Presley’s darker side. However, as a celebration of the ultimate cultural icon, Baz Luhrmann has made one of the most entertaining films of the summer.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: Studio pictures this formally and aesthetically out-there are rare– think the Wachowskis’ Speed Racer or, less charitably, Cats– and, for its many faults, I wouldn’t dream of dissuading someone from gawking at this thing on a gigantic screen.
reviews.author: Oscar Goff

reviews.text: Presleyologists will learn nothing here, and purists will find plenty against which to rail. Less knowing viewers, however, may well be sucked in by Luhrmann’s lively telling of the tale.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: Instead of dramatizing this subject’s life, it dramatizes the extravagance of moviemaking.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: Say this for "Elvis": It is never boring. But it also tells us virtually nothing about Presley.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: Elvis is a compelling watch, with all the glitz and glamor you'd expect for a Presley biopic, but it skews more towards an ode to Luhrmann's cinematic style than an ode to the King.
reviews.author: Jennifer Bisset

reviews.text: Retro looks kill when the king of rock and roll gets the royal treatment from director Baz Luhrmann.
reviews.author: Andiee Paviour

reviews.text: Thanks to [Austin Butler's] blistering on-stage performance, shaken hips and all, the movie's gig sequences feel like Elvis hasn't ever left the building.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: Luhrmann’s “subtlety is for cowards” approach still impresses, and it’s appropriate we got a new film from him at a time when many pundits are pontificating on the nature of “maximalist” (aka as subtle as a brick to the face) cinema.
reviews.author: Travis Johnson

reviews.text: "Elvis” is a whirlwind and not without its flaws. Yet it’s never less than captivating, capturing the singer’s energy while telling his story with the respect it deserves, thrilling and moving the viewer in equal measure.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: You will walk away from 'Elvis' entirely entertained but not exactly educated or enlightened. Regardless, it's never dull and the truly breathtaking performance of Austin Butler is worth the price of admission alone.
reviews.author: Doug Jamieson

reviews.text: Butler’s star-making performance will please everyone, regardless of what you think of the film.
reviews.author: Dustin Chase

reviews.text: Never before has a movie spent such a disproportionate amount of time on a white man doing nothing about the civil rights movement.
reviews.author: Radheyan Simonpillai

reviews.text: “Elvis” is an entertaining fantasy that will keep your toes tapping, whether you’re a fan of “The King” or not.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: Luhrmann’s energy quickly dissipates to reveal a boring, tin-eared and awkward biopic that is mostly by the numbers.
reviews.author: Rob Dean

reviews.text: It’s a film that’s loud and excessive and bloated and colorful and it fits its subject as perfectly as a bedazzled jumpsuit.
reviews.author: Michael Guarnieri

reviews.text: For all its flaws, Elvis remains a remarkably entertaining experience, the credit for which rests largely with its star. Butler is the strongest element film, and the energy with which he infuses the musical numbers is undeniably electrifying.
reviews.author: Brent Hankins

reviews.text: Butler admirably performs his own vocals for the early Presley tunes and sings blended with the King during later acts. Whether die-hard fans or casual viewers can spot the difference barely matters: Butler bets big and wins.
reviews.author: Pat Mullen

reviews.text: When one politically powerful white man claps eyes on the gyrating young Elvis, he asks, “What in God’s sweet name am I looking at?” This remarkable movie suggests one possible answer is the future, in more ways than one.
reviews.author: Stephen Romei

reviews.text: Luhrmann sees Elvis as a mythic American figure or maybe even a full-on superhero — and he positions the tone of his film accordingly, somewhere between Orson Welles’ "Citizen Kane" and Sam Raimi’s "Spider-Man" trilogy.
reviews.author: Caroline Siede

reviews.text: A life of the singer in the form of a portrait of an outsider, a crack at a personality behind layers and layers of feral, restless syncopation and who feeling empty to the end of his days, ever shoulders the mantel of persona and performance.
reviews.author: Ray Pride

reviews.text: Luhrmann eschews the stripped-down plodding and formulaic approach that many historical biopics follow and focuses instead on what he does best, his ability to excite and entice. With frenetic and pulsating almost religious moments, he utilizes pop-like
reviews.author: Taylor Baker

reviews.text: Bloated, gaudy and at times bordering on self-parody. Those missteps, courtesy of director Baz Luhrmann and an ill-used Tom Hanks, squander Austin Butler's brilliant moments in the title role, which deserve a much better movie.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: Elvis blends the energetic and glittery styles of Luhrmann and the captivating and rockin’ performance of Austin Butler.
reviews.author: John Nguyen

reviews.text: Mr. Luhrmann’s film, in keeping with his cartoonist’s soul, is less a tragedy than a 2.5 hour Looney Tunes offering, with Parker as Bugs Bunny forever outwitting the Elmer Fudd-ish Elvis.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: The perfect example of how easy it can be to overlook a film’s flaws when it gets what’s important right, when the experience is so captivating, and when the lead delivers an out-of-this-world performance!
reviews.author: Marianna Neal

reviews.text: [The story is] remarkably engaging, remarkably human, and used Baz Luhrmann's energy to push the film forward at a pace I enjoyed.
reviews.author: Jeremy Jahns

reviews.text: This movie assumes you do not care or know very much about the man who ruled pop music before the coming of The Beatles... Luhrmann treats Presley's life story as a superhero myth, a journey to be savoured on its own.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: If [Lurhmann’s] mission statement as an artist is to restate the importance of the art he’s always loved to new crowds and enable older folks to see it in a new fashion, then this is his most vital film since Romeo and Juliet. Return of the King, indeed.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: Butler as Elvis is phenomenal, while Hanks, under a kilo of prosthetics, still convinces and appals as Parker. But I walked out feeling that the bothersome realities of real-life had been too much to overcome.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: Baz Luhrmann’s Elvis is big, glossy, rollicking, intermittently entertaining and easy to figure out.
reviews.author: Kelly Vance

reviews.text: It still sports Luhrmann’s somewhat frantic style, but it is creative and entertaining.
reviews.author: Diane Carson

reviews.text: No matter the interpretation, the power of a myth like this never left the building.
reviews.author: Eric Webb

reviews.text: Rides on Luhrmann’s talent as a visual artist, and an absolutely stellar titular performance from Austin Butler.
reviews.author: Dan Scully

reviews.text: With Elvis, Luhrmann gives the old bazzle-dazzle to what is perhaps his most iconic subject yet.
reviews.author: Keva York

reviews.text: The glossy visuals and breakneck pacing sap the emotional power from what should be a sympathetic and engaging profile.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: Exhilarating! Butler is a revelation.
reviews.author: Linda Marric

reviews.text: It features some fully engaging and wildly imaginative recreations of famous songs that are simply mesmerizing to behold.
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: Luhrmann uses loads of razzle-dazzle to tell—and sell—this frenetic, whiplash, time-jumping, hyper-stylish fantasia that depicts Elvis’ career as it builds to a crescendo—then progressively consumes him.
reviews.author: Neil Pond

reviews.text: You can’t help falling in love with Austin Butler.
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: Austin Butler catapults to stardom with a lightning in a bottle performance. If only Elvis were the star of his own biopic. A fat suit and prosthetics clad Tom Hanks takes center stage as the lecherous Colonel Tom Parker.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: This flamboyant, dazzling, cinematic spectacle is an unforgettable film about the beloved cultural icon and American music legend. This is one thrilling movie for Elvis fans.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: Elvis has highs and it has lows, but if you are a fan of the singer, you probably won’t want to miss it.
reviews.author: JimmyO

reviews.text: Between Luhrmann’s interesting decision to focus on the singer’s relationship with his manager and Butler’s outstanding performance makes this a one-ticket that is worth the price of admission.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: my expectations for “Elvis” were pretty low. Fortunately for me, Luhrmann exceeded my expectations.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: Elvis may be a bit too frantic and stylistic for its own good, but the movie is ridiculously entertaining. Most of the highs are due a legendary performance from Austin Butler. He is on another level here, and every frame is elevated when he is on screen.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: This zany biopic has its longueurs and is no more historically reliable than you’d expect. Still, as an antipodean fever dream it’s significantly more compelling than previous Luhrmann follies like The Great Gatsby or Australia.
reviews.author: Jake Wilson

reviews.text: Baz Luhrmann’s Elvis is as powerful, passionate and problematic as the man himself. Don’t be afraid to get caught in its trap.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: A good movie, not a great one, but Austin Butler busts this movie through the stratosphere when Elvis takes the stage.
reviews.author: Dan Murrell

reviews.text: There are some definite problems with the film’s over-stuffed length, awkward transitions and uneven pacing. Butler hits it out of the park, but  Luhrman designed this spectacle to make you respect and appreciate Elvis.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: A typical Luhrmann film: lush, grandiose, epic, stylish to the millionth degree.
reviews.author: Tim Stegall

reviews.text: It accomplishes what it sets out to do in reminding audiences of the power of Elvis Presley. He's Romeo or Gatsby or Satine at the Moulin Rouge. He's impossible to ignore. With Butler as his copilot, Luhrmann sets loins afire.
reviews.author: Esther Zuckerman

reviews.text: Regardless of its qualitative merits ... there’s an intensity to the vision here that feels all too lacking in contemporary blockbusters of this size and scale.
reviews.author: Paul Attard

reviews.text: For most of the movie, Luhrmann fillets incident into montage, his slice-and-dice approach thwarting any possible momentum; we long for a scene that lasts more than ten seconds.
reviews.author: Ryan Gilbey

reviews.text: "Elvis" is able to overcome a good number of its flaws and hiccups by the sheer ferocity of Butler's performance and Luhrmann's dogged determination to entertain.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: Austin Butler eerily captures the essence of the King of Rock and Roll. Tom Hanks trails clouds of sulfur as Mephistophelean Col. Tom Parker.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: It's not reality, purely wishful thinking.  [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Martínez

reviews.text: [It] doesn't just fail at making the so-called King of Rock and Roll into a three-dimensional human being; it actively plunges him further into the recesses of memedom, while making his legacy out to be far less interesting than it actually is.
reviews.author: Aisha Harris

reviews.text: In the end, Elvis is not a perfect film. But it's certainly not a bad one either. Far from it. Luhrmann asks for our investment of time and energy, of which you'll need plenty of both to keep up with everything he throws at us with this one.
reviews.author: Lisa Trifone

reviews.text: You may even be begging: Baz, come on, just hold still. But no, we’re off again. I’ve had fever dreams that have been less delirious. But on the plus side, even if it’s never deep or enlightening, it has a fizzing energy.
reviews.author: Deborah Ross

reviews.text: A tacky, towering monolith of gaudy overkill and excess — as any film about Elvis Presley should rightfully be.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: This movie isn't actually about Elvis, but his career. Austin Butler has a star turn as Elvis, and Tom Hanks is mesmerizing - yet at almost 3 hours it still feels like so much of Elvis' story is missing. Still, the movie is a fascinating look at showbiz.
reviews.author: Grace Randolph

reviews.text: Elvis so mythologizes the music biopic that after a sequence where Elvis thrusts his pelvis, and girls scream tears of unbridled desire in slow motion shots, you'd be forgiven for thinking the singer had invented sex itself.
reviews.author: David Crow

reviews.text: Elvis is glitz, spectacle, magnanimous performances and a born superstar in Austin Butler, who is the singular subject that will be discussed on loop.  With every fiber of his being, Butler brings Elvis to life with electrifying magnificence!
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: [An] overstuffed ode to a pop culture icon is just as sparkly and blisteringly paced as you’d expect... somehow still manages to paint only the shallowest portrait of a deeply complicated man with a very conflicted existence.
reviews.author: J Hurtado

reviews.text: This isn’t a bad movie by any stretch, but it’s too long and should have been way better, given the opportunity presented. Alas.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: I’ve spent a lot of time thinking about Elvis. “Elvis,” for all its flaws and compromises, made me want to listen to him, as if for the first time.
reviews.author: A.O. Scott

reviews.text: A very conventional and very overstuffed biopic.
reviews.author: Matt Singer

reviews.text: Despite ... some unformed or clunky notions about the icon's cultural impact, Elvis is a big, bold, and just-unconventional-enough piece of biography.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Austin Butler gives a rounded performance that transcends an impersonation of a man who spawned a generation (or two) of impersonators.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: There are aspects of Elvis that is cinematic mastery and there are other parts that is bilge. It’s a mess of contradictions as well as being… just a mess.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: It is three films battling it out with one another for much of the runtime, but it’s still so much better than one could have hoped for.
reviews.author: Jason Shawhan

reviews.text: Luhrmann is nothing if not one of the most enthusiastic film showmen. And this is never so clear as when he hits the first half-hour of Elvis out of the park. Its pace, at least in the early going, is breathless.
reviews.author: Jim Slotek

reviews.text: From Elvis' origins as poor white trash in Memphis to the biggest musical act in the world, it’s all here in a raw onslaught of facts and moments. Forget about insight; this barely leaves audiences time to think
reviews.author: Anthony Morris

reviews.text: Visually dazzling biopic of Elvis Presley, but its subject remains maddeningly out of focus.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: The result is a dizzying, almost hallucinatory experience — akin to being thrown into a washing machine and mercilessly churned for 2 1/2 hours.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: “Elvis” worships its subject, but beneath that worship is a condescension, presumably unconscious, that borders on contempt. Or perhaps the contempt is for itself.
reviews.author: Mark Feeney

reviews.text: God, the film can be weird. Yet in its cartoonish frenzy, Luhrmann does actually capture how thrilling and subversive the early Presley must have been.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: An overflow of colors, music, & history told so frenetically that at times I almost asked them to pause the presentation...but should be enjoyed as it is, allowing oneself to be enveloped by a thousand images of madness, debauchery & excess.
reviews.author: Jorge Rivera Rubio

reviews.text: I don't even like Elvis Presley, but I would watch this film again just to see Austin Butler's performance. Tom Hanks, on the other hand, is a caricature.
reviews.author: Korey Coleman

reviews.text: Less a conventional biographical movie than a flamboyant Baz Luhrmann fantasia on the rise and fall of Elvis Presley, an exercise in sensory overload that’s fascinating but exhausting.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Elvis is structured like a nearly three-hour sizzle reel. It doesn’t so much have scenes as suites. It moves.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: A kaleidoscopic, immersive experience in a story many of us have not heard before, making every one of its 159 minutes riveting. That’s no easy feat.
reviews.author: Lisa Johnson Mandell

reviews.text: The film’s preference for speed over soul is exhausting and irritating, but it’s not without its pleasures.
reviews.author: Bennett Campbell Ferguson

reviews.text: You spend the first half in awe of Baz but the second in awe of Butler, and that’s a compliment to both.
reviews.author: CJ Johnson

reviews.text: Quite a cinematic achievement whose positive values far outweigh any issues some might have with Luhrmann’s non-conformist approach with Elvis’ life and career.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: Butler's got the voice and swagger down and even does most of his singing throughout the film. More importantly, the 30-year-old actor captures Elvis’ tender effect, his sly carnality, and painfully gullible naivete.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: The vibrant biopic Elvis continues filmmaker Baz Luhrmann's pattern of making a protagonist’s life story look like a manic-energy carnival. The musical numbers are fantastic, but viewers should expect a very glossy version of Elvis Presley’s life.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: This is everything you might expect of a Baz Luhrmann biopic. It’s brash, loud, maximalist, and certainly never boring, but also keeps its subject at a distance, enthralled by his glamour not his soul.
reviews.author: Olly Richards

reviews.text: an explosion of visuals, often in split screens, where recurring circular motifs plunge spinning roulette wheels into the depths of Parker’s eye and Ferris wheels morph into record labels whirling on a turntable
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: Elvis services neither the hardcore fans who grew up on his music, a younger generation that might be interested in learning more about the mythical musical figure, or film buffs who have enjoyed Luhrmann’s previous movies.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: Luhrmann's ELVIS is less a straight-forward admiring biopic than a magical fairy-tale built around the complicated relationship between the singer and his shady manager.
reviews.author: Cate Marquis

reviews.text: Elvis is a biopic through and through, well set in his era, highlighting what the king of rock did for social progress from his stage. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Irene Crespo

reviews.text: Lurhmann uses his run time to generate a hurricane of emotion and information, attempting to treat the story of Elvis Presley as a pop tragedy with a side of sensorial assault.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Ultimately, your reaction to Elvis is going to depend on whether or not you can vibrate on Luhrmann’s frequency.
reviews.author: Chris McCoy

reviews.text: Elvis may not be breaking too much new ground, but between the fun of the singer’s early days and the growth of his character in the later stages of his short life, not even Colonel Tom Parker can stand in the way of what works best about this film.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: It’s overstuffed, bloated, and succumbs to trite biopic decisions.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: A rapturous, rhapsodic tour de force that serves up a dizzying, breathlessly paced biographical portrait..All up, Luhrmann and his team have done a splendid job with 'Elvis', an audacious biopic designed to enthrall non-fans as much as his devotees.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: An artistic milestone retold as a uniquely American tragedy.
reviews.author: Scott Mendelson

reviews.text: A cradle-to-the-grave biopic of the king of rock ’n’ roll whose sad and tragic end as a Las Vegas cash cow provides a Gatsby-esque critique of the self-mythologising nature of the American Dream.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: …could still have used a little more musical action and a little less financial conversation…
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: The Elvis Presley story told as Moulin Rouge. Director Baz Luhrmann uses his most flamboyant techniques to capture the energy of the flamboyant legend.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: Processing such delirium, "Elvis" is an opus of exhaustion. Luhrmann’s fever dream veers from campfire fable to therapy session and is as gaudy as its subject.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: It is a movie about the person who was Elvis’ biggest fan (in this conceit) and the many ways he saw Elvis, his glory and his simple humanity.
reviews.author: David Poland

reviews.text: “Elvis” isn’t just a reinvigoration of the Elvis myth, it’s a resurrection of the King himself. Left the building? Not if Baz Luhrmann has anything to say about it.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: Stunning visuals as expected. Austin Butler's performance as Elvis is magnetic. He radiates on screen! I expect to see his name during award season for best actor.
reviews.author: Wendy Lee Szany

reviews.text: “Elvis” benefits from Luhrman's direction and rebellion against traditional biography rubric. However, the last section of the film falls into repetitiveness and finishes in the same place where most music icons' biographies end. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juanma Fernández París

reviews.text: “Elvis” is like watching a good Elvis impersonator, not really like watching the King himself.
reviews.author: Scott Greenstone

reviews.text: At 2 hours and 40 minutes, there's a lot to pack into Baz Luhrmann's Elvis given it covers the King's entire life. The film covers Elvis' life with grace due to Luhrmann's swift moving direction and a stellar performance by Austin Butler.
reviews.author: Lee McCoy

reviews.text: It’s extraordinary how Luhrmann is able to tell this story honestly, while still making it palatable. It’s equally extraordinary that he can take this short and tragically misdirected life and make it feel like a triumph.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: Luhrmann cannot hide his love for the King of Rock and Roll, and never once attempts any kind of unbiased examination. But if you know that going in, Elvis becomes much larger than the sum of its parts, much like Presley himself.
reviews.author: Alan Cerny

reviews.text: A golden fantasy, an impetuous look at key points [in the life] of the legend that doesn't avoid grey zones -infidelity and drugs- without exploiting gruesome details. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Loser

reviews.text: An overlong, narrative mess as excessive as one of the King's fried peanut butter and banana sandwiches. However, with Butler’s stellar portrayal, it’s never dull, and more enjoyable than not.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: What disappoints the most is that Luhrmann’s wild visuals and use of Parker’s subjectivity (a colossally misguided Hanks performance) don’t distract from Elvis’ formulaic biopic structure. It’s the same old story, except bedazzled into an eyesore.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: One might say I couldn’t help falling in love with this film...
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: While every big swing isn’t perfect, nobody is ever going to say that Baz Luhrmann did The King an injustice.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: Bludgeons one into submission with a never-ending vortex of over-directed shallow stylistic insanity. But Austin Butler is going to be a star.
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: We get no real insight into the internal lives of either characters; there’s an emptiness to the film when Elvis is not on stage. That could be the point of the movie, but it never acknowledges it.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: [Baz Luhrmann's] sumptuous tribute to the iconic performer is at its best when Austin Butler’s seen on stage, giving over his body to the music, and making audiences believe Elvis hasn’t yet left the building.
reviews.author: Rebecca Murray

reviews.text: Baz Luhrmann’s Elvis is a bombastic journey about one of music’s greatest artist. Running on 1.21 gigawatts, it’s a vibrant and electric film that could only come from Luhrmann.
reviews.author: David Gonzalez

reviews.text: Few filmakers can portray emotions like Baz Luhrmann. Pleasure, extasy, freedom, disappointment, danger. We feel everything at 200% watching his movies. And he is unchained once again in Elvis, to his fans' joy and his haters' misery.
reviews.author: Jesus Agudo

reviews.text: It's a lot like his later works. It is flinging everything at you. It tries to do too much and takes too long to get there. But underneath all the flourishes and the indulgence, there is still a vitality that cannot be denied.
reviews.author: Brian Lloyd

reviews.text: ...zooms through the King of Rock and Roll’s life as if it were running through a funhouse.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: The first 20 minutes are so dizzying that you say to yourself, OK, if he can keep this up, I’ll buy it. But of course, he can’t sustain his own initial excitement because reality always sets in: what is this movie about, anyway?
reviews.author: Roger Friedman

reviews.text: Admirable acting, beautiful cinematography, and wonky editing. Be prepared for the fast-paced “pop-up book” version of Elvis's life!
reviews.author: Jason Escamilla

reviews.text: Baz Luhrmann’s slightly more restrained style works successfully in service of Butler’s performance, which is sublime in the second half of the movie.
reviews.author: Al Shipley

reviews.text: The film is at its best when it lets [Austin] Butler loose, thrusting, smirking and crooning his way through stunning performance pieces that speaks to the unmatched charisma of Presley and Butler’s respectful manifestation.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: Baz Luhrmann's best film since Moulin Rouge. A delirious, non-stop fever dream that tells the story of the iconic hip-shaking star. Austin Butler delivers a star-turning performance that carries the whole thing. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: “Elvis” is a vibrant film, which is what you would expect from Luhrmann, but what’s most impressive is how he uses the music to take it to the next level.
reviews.author: Mathew DeKinder

reviews.text: [Elvis] is easily [Baz] Lurhmann's most ambitious project to date and the first thing that caught my attention is Austin Butler's stunning performance in the title role.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: Elvis is too long, too melodramatic, too everything. But it’s also often wildly entertaining.
reviews.author: Max Weiss

reviews.text: A grand cinematic spectacle that intelligently breaks away from cliches and vulgarity with its opulent aesthetic. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: The protracted rubbernecking at Elvis’s inexorable decline epitomizes a film that regularly backs away from its keenest observations about the icon to merely, and superficially, bask in his star power.
reviews.author: Jake Cole

reviews.text: With Luhrmann’s films, he almost always wants to create an extravagant fairy tale, and while that approach tonally mostly makes sense with the life of Presley, Luhrmann’s musical biopic Elvis becomes more style than substance.
reviews.author: Ross Bonaime

reviews.text: It takes time to warm up but Elvis provides audiences with a celebratory tribute to an iconic musician. At the very least, see it for Austin Butler's performance!
reviews.author: Matthew Toomey

reviews.text: By bringing out Elvis’ humanity and how his identity was shaped, Butler puts an indelible stamp on one of the 20th century’s brightest supernovas. Dynamic in song, movement, and demeanor, the actor is mesmerizing in a classic “star is born” scenario.
reviews.author: Lynn Venhaus

reviews.text: Even with the razzle-dazzle Baz factor, this film was always going to rise or fall on its Elvis and Austin Butler is quite simply a sensation, bringing the King back to big-screen life with a riveting rock 'n roll performance.
reviews.author: Kate Rodger

reviews.text: If you’re after revelation and intrigue, that’s in short supply in this Wikipedia odyssey through the career of the most successful recording artist to ever walk the Earth.
reviews.author: Tom Beasley

reviews.text: Never anything less than a feast for the eyes.
reviews.author: Jayne Nelson

reviews.text: It’s big. It’s bold. It’s brash. It’s brassy. And yet, it’s nothin’ but a blue-suede snooze.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: Everything you expect from a Luhrmann film is put on display within the first ten minutes, but taken up to a hundred, with every aspect maximalist to the extreme.
reviews.author: Alysha Prasad

reviews.text: A fittingly over the top tribute to one of the most famous people in entertainment history, but perhaps arrives 20 years later than it should, given how much time has passed.
reviews.author: George Simpson

reviews.text: Judging by the sneers of some critics during the screening, it´s disappointing to realize people either lost the ability to appreciate disciplined excess or resigned themselves to the safety of commonplace. [Full review in Portuguese]
reviews.author: Pablo Villaça

reviews.text: A sharp edit away from being a classic, Elvis is an exhilarating look at one of America’s most iconic figures, powered by Baz Luhrmann’s exhilarating direction and Austin Butler’s astonishing lead performance.
reviews.author: Luke Walpole

reviews.text: Baz Luhrmann’s “Elvis” is more than all right, mama. It blasts the screen with the Aussie director’s trademark glitter and bravado but also hits the right historical and musical notes for a biopic worthy of a legendary performer.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: A splashy biopic that's all sizzle and no fire.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: Raw, gyrating machismo turned Elvis into a god with the power to bring teenyboppers to instantaneous orgasm with a swing of the hips. Under Luhrmann's unthrottled tutelage, that overwhelming dynamo of charisma is made merely loud.
reviews.author: Charles Bramesco

reviews.text: It’s tough to watch a movie like Elvis and totally dismiss it, no matter how much of a trainwreck it might seem.
reviews.author: Luke Hicks

reviews.text: It lurches about flashing its gold like a drunk old millionaire.
reviews.author: Caspar Salmon

reviews.text: What happens when the director of Moulin Rouge! makes a film about Elvis? A lot of shake, rattle and razzmatazz.
reviews.author: Anna Smith

reviews.text: It would be fair to conclude that Elvis would have benefited from a little more restraint and sobriety. The picture would then have been infinitely less blurry and far more memorable.
reviews.author: Saibal Chatterjee

reviews.text:
A memorable, and brilliant movie.
[Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Àngel Quintana

reviews.text: Baz Luhrmann restores The King to his throne in this subjective but generous, imaginative and visually opulent biopic.
reviews.author: Stephen Dalton

reviews.text: A spectacle as much as a story. Elvis's life, all shook up.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: While there’s an argument that Luhrmann’s Elvis is all show and no tell, it’s such a dazzling performance from the Australian director that it’s hard to begrudge any fleck of superficiality.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: Hanks’s unusually generous serving of ham is balanced out by a sincere and overall impressive Austin Butler in the title role.
reviews.author: Adam Solomons

reviews.text: Butler sparkles like a rhinestoned jumpsuit in this role as he nails Elvis' signature drawl, cadence, physicality, and gyrating stage presence.
reviews.author: Luke Hearfield

reviews.text: It’s obviously too early to call these things but I would be surprised if Elvis doesn’t factor prominently in the next Oscar race.
reviews.author: Zhuo-Ning Su

reviews.text: As a strict 100% factual biopic, Elvis is probably a failure. But as a biography of an idea, it’s as much a triumph as you could hope for, a work of controlled and sustained mad love for an artist whose story is never-ending.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: Elvis is the Baz Luhrmanniest film Baz Luhrmann has made yet.
reviews.author: Rafael Motamayor

reviews.text: Surface-level take on The King, but a great time nonetheless.
reviews.author: Anna Bogutskaya

reviews.text: Baz Luhrmann's loving tribute to  EP, told though the unreliable narration of Hanks as Col. Tom. Austin Butler is a revelation, and through use of kinetic music style vitalizes Presley's inherent excitement and perhaps his continuing legacy
reviews.author: Jason Gorber

reviews.text: When Austin Butler shakes his hips in Elvis’s first gig as a full-blown rock ‘n’ roller, it’s like watching two stars being born.
reviews.author: Philip De Semlyen

reviews.text: It may well be a star-making turn for [Austin Butler], a bold announcement of thespian vigor and ingenuity that even devoted fans of The Carrie Diaries didn’t know he had. A shame, then, that Luhrmann works so hard to drown him out.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: To complain that “Elvis” is basically a compilation of musical-biopic conventions is a bit like complaining about a greatest-hits album; it also misses... [Luhrmann’s] ability to suffuse clichés with sincerity, energy and feeling.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: Butler nails the moves, the mannerisms, the soulful voice and somehow even channels the icon’s charisma. When girls scream at him in the film’s electrifying musical sequences, you wonder how much acting was required.
reviews.author: Andy Lea

reviews.text: You can’t help falling in love with this shake, rattle and roll through the life of the biggest star the world has ever seen.
reviews.author: Dulcie Pearce

reviews.text: There’s enough energy and flash... to overcome most nit-picking, and Butler throws himself into a performance that’s wildly physical but never cartoonish or disrespectful.
reviews.author: Steve Pond

reviews.text: As it is, this is just another exercise in Elvis impersonation, its upper lip twitching to no purpose.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: Luhrmann has never been an accomplished dramatist. He has the instincts of a pop video supremo. And in pop god Elvis Presley he may have found his perfect subject.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: [Butler's] keen instinct for melodrama and burn-the-screen-down charisma give his Elvis a midcentury Method-acting rawness.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: The toe-tapping beats of this full-throated biopic will be familiar in more ways than one but Baz Luhrmann, like Elvis, knows how to put on a great show. Butler’s Best Actor chatter starts here.
reviews.author: Jordan Farley

reviews.text: While you won’t find all that much truth in Baz Luhrmann’s cradle-to-grave dramatisation of his life, the Australian filmmaker has delivered something far more compelling: an American fairytale.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: Sometimes Elvis feels like a lost Oliver Stone film from his daring 1990s heyday: a big-canvas exploration of debauched American appetites.
reviews.author: Joshua Rothkopf

reviews.text: A fizzy, delirious, impishly energized, compulsively watchable 2-hour-and-39-minute fever dream -- a spangly pinwheel of a movie that converts the Elvis saga we all carry around in our heads into a lavishly staged biopic-as-pop-opera.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: If the writing too seldom measures up to the astonishing visual impact, the affinity the director feels for his showman subject is both contagious and exhausting.
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: Baz Luhrmann's Elvis is a dizzying and at times even overwhelming chronicle of the rock icon. Austin Butler is stellar as Elvis, giving it his absolute all in every scene; truly, a star is born here.
reviews.author: Jim Vejvoda

reviews.text: It finds so little reason for Presley’s life to be the stuff of a Baz Luhrmann movie that the equation ultimately inverts itself, leaving us with an Elvis Presley movie about Baz Luhrmann. They both deserve better.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: Perhaps more than anyone who has seriously taken on Elvis, Butler thrillingly succeeds, especially in the film’s first half, with an authentic rhythm that makes us wonder what greater heights Elvis could have climbed.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: Luhrmann’s colourful house style can be frantic and shallow, but his desire to get our knickers in a twist, here, feels honest-to-god urgent. This is the most substantial thing he’s done since Romeo + Juliet.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

synopsis: The film explores the life and music of Elvis Presley (Austin Butler), seen through the prism of his complicated relationship with his enigmatic manager, Colonel Tom Parker (Tom Hanks). The story delves into the complex dynamic between Presley and Parker spanning over 20 years, from Presley's rise to fame to his unprecedented stardom, against the backdrop of the evolving cultural landscape and loss of innocence in America. Central to that journey is one of the most significant and influential people in Elvis's life, Priscilla Presley (Olivia DeJonge).
